$comment: What each runtime accepts as a host-run <invoke>'s `_sce_deadline_ms` <param>, one table for every backend.

A <param expr> reaches the request as the TEXT of its value, so the grammar is over text: one or more ASCII digits, optionally followed by '.' and one or more '0' (a script engine may render a whole number `5000.0`), and nothing else - no sign, no whitespace, no exponent, no digit separator.
The value must fit a signed 64-bit count of milliseconds, the widest type every runtime's clock arithmetic shares.

Written out rather than left to each language's number parser, because those disagree: Go reads hex floats, Python reads `1_000` and non-ASCII digits, and each trims a different set of whitespace. A deadline one backend honours and another refuses would make the same document behave differently by where it was compiled.
`accepted` pairs are [written, milliseconds], with the milliseconds as a string so no JSON reader rounds them.
